explanation: What the West India Company took in 1630 was not an empty coast. It was a royal colony with a capital, a government, a church and a working sugar economy — the thing the captaincies had failed to produce and the crown had installed in 1549. A colony is worth conquering when somebody else has already built it, and the Company took the built part: at its height it held almost half of the settled European area of Brazil, with its headquarters at Recife.
